content: Calcium carbonate is a dietary supplement that is prescribed when the amount of calcium obtained through the diet is insufficient. Calcium is essential for maintaining healthy bones, muscles, the nervous system, and the heart. Additionally, calcium carbonate is used as an antacid to alleviate symptoms such as heartburn, acid indigestion, and stomach upset. This medication is available both with and without a prescription. In some cases, it may be prescribed for other purposes; consult your doctor or pharmacist for further information. Calcium carbonate is available in various forms, including tablets, chewable tablets, capsules, and liquid, and is taken orally. It is typically taken three or four times a day. Follow the instructions provided on your prescription or package label carefully, and ask your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take calcium carbonate exactly as directed. Do not take more or less of it, or take it more frequently than prescribed by your doctor. When using this medication as a dietary supplement, take it with food or after meals. Chewable tablets must be chewed thoroughly before swallowing; do not swallow them whole. After taking regular or chewable tablets or capsules, drink a full glass of water. Some liquid forms of calcium carbonate require thorough shaking before use. Do not use calcium carbonate as an antacid for more than two weeks unless directed by your doctor. Before taking calcium carbonate, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to calcium carbonate or any other medications. Provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are currently taking, especially digoxin (Lanoxin), etidronate (Didronel), phenytoin (Dilantin), tetracycline (Sumycin), and vitamins. Avoid taking calcium carbonate within 1-2 hours of other medications, as calcium may reduce their effectiveness. Inform your doctor if you have or have ever had kidney disease or stomach conditions. Additionally, let your doctor know if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. If you become pregnant while taking calcium carbonate, contact your doctor immediately. If you are taking calcium carbonate on a regular schedule and miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Calcium carbonate may cause side effects. Notify your doctor if you experience any of the following symptoms, especially if they are severe or persistent: upset stomach, vomiting, stomach pain, belching, constipation, dry mouth, increased urination, loss of appetite, or a metallic taste. Store this medication in the container it came in, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (do not store it in the bathroom). Dispose of any outdated or no longer needed medication properly. Consult your pharmacist for guidance on proper disposal. In case of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. If this medication has been prescribed for you, ensure you attend all scheduled appointments with your doctor so your response to calcium carbonate can be monitored. Do not share your medication with anyone else.
